source.report_note: Limits are those of the manufacturer's tables (Fluke 175 / 177 / 179 Calibration Information, Table 2 pp. 10-11 for the 175, Table 3 pp. 12-13 for the 177 / 179) with three corrections to misprints: 175 ohms 500 ohm upper limit (printed 504.7 kOhm, used 504.7 ohm); 177 / 179 AC volts 5 V 45 Hz upper limit (printed 5.103 V, used 5.053 V, 1.0 % + 3 counts); 177 / 179 DC volts frequency (printed 3 V 45 kHz with the limits 45.06 and 44.94 Hz; used 3 V at 45 Hz, 44.94 to 45.06 Hz).
source.note: Table 2 (175: 52 rows) and Table 3 (177 / 179: 51 rows, plus 3 temperature rows for the 179 only): 175 / 177 / 179 Calibration Information pp. 10-13. The tables have no step numbers: steps are numbered in table order. THREE printed values are corrected (each flagged on the point and on the report): 175 ohms 500 ohm upper limit printed 504.7 kOhm (judged 504.7 ohm); 177/179 AC volts 5 V 45 Hz upper limit printed 5.103 V (judged 5.053 V, 1.0 % + 3 counts); 177/179 DC volts frequency printed "3 V 45 kHz, 45.06 / 44.94 Hz" (judged 3 V at 45 Hz, 44.94 to 45.06 Hz). Ranges are not named in the manual: each shown range is the one the reading falls in (from the published 170 Series resolutions). The manual names a Fluke 5500A; the procedure drives a Fluke 5522A or 5560A (or you set the calibrator by hand). High-voltage points go straight to the test value (the manual prescribes no ramp). The meters have no remote interface: you type the display reading.
